title: USA Edge Mexico 2-1 in Thrilling World Cup 2026 Opener
summary: The United States kicked off the 2026 FIFA World Cup with a dramatic 2-1 victory over rivals Mexico at MetLife Stadium in a pulsating opening match.
content:
The 2026 FIFA World Cup burst into life with a spectacular opening match as the United States defeated Mexico 2-1 at a packed MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. A crowd of 82,500 witnessed a fierce CONCACAF rivalry deliver everything it promised and more on the grandest stage of all.

First Half Fireworks

The hosts wasted no time settling nerves, with Christian Pulisic unlocking the Mexican defence in the 18th minute. A slick one-two with Gio Reyna on the edge of the box gave Pulisic the half-yard he needed, and his curling effort beat Guillermo Ochoa at the near post. Mexico responded with sustained pressure, and Hirving Lozano forced a sharp save from Matt Turner before Santiago Gimenez equalized in the 37th minute with a towering header from Edson Alvarez's pinpoint free kick.

Weah Strikes the Winner

The second half was a tense tactical battle, with both managers making calculated adjustments. Gregg Berhalter introduced Folarin Balogun on the hour mark, and the substitution injected fresh energy into the American attack. The decisive moment arrived in the 74th minute when Timothy Weah latched onto a defence-splitting pass from Weston McKennie, drove into the penalty area, and slotted the ball past Ochoa with composure beyond his years.

Defensive Resilience

The final fifteen minutes were a test of character for the USA. Mexico threw bodies forward in search of an equalizer, with Raul Jimenez and Jesus Corona combining dangerously. However, the American backline, marshalled superbly by Chris Richards and Antonee Robinson, held firm. Turner made one crucial fingertip save in stoppage time to preserve the lead and send the stadium into raptures.

What It Means

The result gives the United States a perfect start to their home World Cup campaign and puts them top of Group B with three points. Mexico, meanwhile, face a must-win encounter against Ecuador in their next fixture. With 48 teams competing across 16 venues in the expanded tournament format, every point is vital in determining which sides progress from the group stage.
